- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above true outcome, reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days; if below, add 0.5–1% if sentiment is bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.67), model often misreads trend; use 3-period moving average of sentiment to guide correction.  
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
